Smokeskin-Willer

Milar Maryon says that his restorative supplies are running low and asked me to collect 5 portions each of bloat and scrib jelly from one of the nearby kwama colonies: Mudan-Mul Egg Mine or Sinarralit Egg Mine. He needs them for Smokeskin-Killer who, he confided, is a veteran of the Arnesian War and needs potions of Fortify Willpower to help him deal with the trauma from the experience.
I delivered the bloat and scrib jelly to Milar Maryon. He thanked and rewarded me for my service.
The Domain of Living Fire
I have killed the Flame Monarch underneath Tel Vos. Master Aryon would like to hear of this.
Conserving Water

Master Aryon was irritated that the water supplying his personal conservatory stopped flowing. Not knowing that I was the one who shut it off, he accepted my offer to "fix" the conservatory water supply issue for him.

After restoring the supply to Aryon's conservatory water, I returned to him for my reward. I think he may have suspected that I had some hand in the affair. He gave me the book titled "A Hypothetical Treachery"... I think I caught a hint of a smile as he handed it to me. I do not believe he was entirely displeased with my deceit. But I should plan carefully before I ever attempt to cross him again.
Root of the Problem

A farmer in Vos named Dreynos Elvul told me that a root has broken through the wall of his farmhouse. Apparently this is a common issue in the village. Maybe I can ask around town and see if anyone has ideas.

I spoke to Surin Zabbi in Vos about the mushroom roots from Tel Vos. He suggested that I speak with his wife, Ibanu Zabbi, in Sinarralit Egg Mine. Apparently they rarely see roots there. Maybe she'll have an idea about how to deal with them.

Ibanu Zabbi in Sinarralit Egg Mine informed me that Telvanni mushroom roots are repelled by kwama poison which sometimes fills pools in kwama colonies. Apparently cysts of kwama poison can form on the surface of these pools. I may be able to collect some of them if I am careful. I think Dreynos Elvul is desperate enough to try using it -- three samples should be enough.
I brought enough samples of kwama poison to Dreynos Elvul for him to try removing the Telvanni roots from his house. He suggested that I check back in a week to see if the treatment worked.
I should check in with Dreynos Elvul in Vos about the mushroom roots from Tel Vos which were breaking into his house.
I refused to help Dreynos with his root problem.
The kwama poison worked to wither and repel the Telvanni roots which broke into Dreynos Elvul's house in Vos. He thanked me and gave me a Dwemer artifact as a reward.
The Final Door
Galos Mathendis gave me a list of questions to ask an ashlander scout staying at the Varo Tradehouse in Vos. He insisted that I ask them in the same order in which he wrote them down.
I asked the ashlander scout, Hairan Mannanalit, about Indoranyon like Galos Mathendis asked. I should tell him what she told me.

Galos seemed excited about what I told him. He wishes to go to Indoranyon himself but wants me to make the trip. I think he plans to teleport to me once I get there. He gave me an enchanted scroll and told me to cast it on top of the ruins near the door.

Galos and Milyn met me at Indoranyon. They discussed the next steps for Galos' enchanting research. He asked me to come back to his chambers in Tel Vos in one week. And he would have something for me. I don't understand what is going on and the two wizards wouldn't explain it to me.
It's been one week since I spoke to Galos Mathendis. I should go check on him in the Tel Vos Mouth's Quarters.

When I returned to Galos' chambers, he was gone. I hope that his experiment was successful. I found an inscribed key on a carved medallion on the floor of his room. It had a small tag attached to it which simply read: Indoranyon. Perhaps this key can be used on the door there?
Girith's guar died before I could bring it back to him.
I successfully led Girith's pack guar back to him.
The Eerie Lantern

On the side of the road near Tel Vos, I found an eerie lantern. Perhaps I should have just left it, but I decided to pick it up. When I did, a light appeared and began moving west; further into the Grazelands.

I followed the light and found a lone Ashlander standing on a hilltop. He spoke a language I did not understand, but he kept repeating a single word: "Salkurnudai". He disappeared into the darkness before I could attempt to communicate. One of the local ashlander tribes might know something about this lantern or that word.
The Wise Woman I spoke with asked that I bring the ghost lantern back to her.

I have been tasked by a Wise Woman of the Ashlanders to bring the ghost lantern to an ancient ashlander burial place called Molaguradan. She told me that it is deep underneath Tel Vos and that I should follow a lava river which pours into a dark hole. I was warned NOT to put the lantern away for any reason otherwise the spirit of the Salkurnudai hunter would be lost.
I found the burial cavern within Molaguradan. When I arrived, the ghost lantern left my hand to be held by a mummified ashlander corpse. I feel that I have been empowered by the ashlander spirits.
I stopped carrying the ghost lantern and was immediately attacked by the mad spirit of the Salkurnudai hunter. I have failed my quest to take it to Molaguradan.

I met with an ashlander Wise Woman who told me the man I encountered was an ashlander ancestor spirit. I decided not to help put the spirit of the Salkurnudai tribesman to rest and gave up the lantern.
Let The Ebony Flow
I heard a rumor that Turedus Talanian is looking for a member of House Telvanni to conduct some more work for him.

I agreed to speak to Gulakhan Ashibaal at the Zainab Camp on behalf of Turedus Talanian. He wishes to ensure that the ashlander ebony flows through Tel Vos as part of their trade deal with House Hlaalu.
Ashibaal agreed with my reasoning for the Zainab to conduct their ebony trade with House Hlaalu in Vos. I should report back to Turedus Talanian.
Turedus Talanian was pleased with the results of my ebony trade agreement with the Zainab. He gave me an enchanted ebony ring as a reward.
Imitation is the Sincerest Form of Forgery
Smokeskin-Killer informed me that Master Aryon may be interested in a new addition to the Tel Vos Dwemer Museum.
I agreed to return to Odirniran to find the dwemer device which Milyn Faram has been using to create magical scrolls with. Aryon then wants me to report back to him.
I found the dwemer device in Odirniran, but it is far too large to be moved easily. As soon as I entered the room, however, Milyn Faram appeared behind me.
Milyn Faram discovered me at the dwemer ideographer. He wasn't angry and instead offered a deal with Aryon to sell him the device. I should take the offer back to Aryon.
Aryon agreed to Milyn's terms and will arrange to have the dwemer ideographer moved to Tel Vos. He suggested that I talk to him a week.

Aryon told me that the dwemer ideographer has been installed in his laboratory. Which is located at the top of the second tallest tower in Tel Vos. He said that I can buy some standard blank scrolls from Alenus Vendu in the Services Tower which I will need to use the machine.

While talking to an Ashlander Wise Woman, I learned that the ashlander tribes might be interested in having access to the caverns below Tel Vos, which they refer to as "Molaguradan". The lord of Tel Vos may be interested in this information. Perhaps I can make it worth my while...

While talking to an Ashlander Wise Woman, I learned that the ashlander tribes might be interested in having access to the caverns below Tel Vos, which they refer to as "Molaguradan". Master Aryon in Tel Vos may be interested in this information.
Aryon thanked me for telling him about the ashlanders' interest in accessing Molaguradan underneath Tel Vos.

I agreed to banish the Flame Monarch in the caverns of Molaguradan underneath Tel Vos for Aryon. He suggested I speak with his retainers in the services tower to obtain better equipment. He also requested that I bring back an artifact to prove that I defeated the Flame Monarch.

Aryon was grateful that I banished the Flame Monarch underneath Tel Vos. In return, he said that his retainers in the services tower would offer me better rates. He also gave me some powerful potions. I think they may work well with the sword I found.
Waxing Pathetic Scamps

Galos Mathendis asked me to get 10 scraps of scamp skin for him. He plans to render scamp tallow from it to make special enchanting candles to help with his enchanting research in Tel Vos. He mentioned that Felara Andrethi in Tel Aruhn generally keeps some in stock. Otherwise I can hunt scamp in Daedric shrines.

I successfully delivered the scraps of scamp skin to Galos Mathendis for his enchanting research. He plans to render scamp tallow from it. He said that once he finishes, I can expect to make better enchantments on his table.
A Lesson in Thieving

Galos Mathendis has asked me to obtain a copy of "The Final Lesson" book for him. He mentioned that he has seen two copies recently. One in Gothren's tower in Tel Aruhn and another, owned by Endar Drenim in Neloth's tower, Tel Naga, in Sadrith Mora. He gave me a potion of Invisibility to help with my quest.
I obtained a copy of "The Final Lesson" for Galos Mathendis. He thanked me and gave me something he enchanted as a reward.
Galos gave me some training in enchanting as a reward for finding "The Final Lesson" for his enchanting research.
Galos gave me a soul gem filled with something called a "Verminoth". He mentioned that he thought it might have wandered up from passages below the tower.
Enchanted Quill Acquaintances
Galos Mathendis asked me to deliver a letter to Milyn Faram in Odirniran. Something to do with his enchanting research.
Milyn Faram read the letter from Galos Mathendis and asked me to tell him that he "understands". And gave me an inscribed key to bring back to Galos.
Galos Mathendis was pleased with the key I brought him from Milyn Faram. He gave me an enchanted amulet as a reward.
I have agreed to try and hunt down the missing guar hides for Athanden Girith. He also asked me to bring his pack guar back safely. It will be best to check with the local Ashlanders first.
A Smidge Too Far

I came across a Breton trader in Tel Mora who was afflicted by a curse of paralysis after angering Mistress Dratha. He asked me to help him remove the curse and suggested that I ask around town. He said that Kirsty brought him some food and may be willing to help more.
I talked to Kirsty in Tel Mora who said she can't help but suggested that I talk to Master Aryon in Tel Vos who may be able to remove the Breton trader's curse of paralysis.

Master Aryon agreed to help the paralyzed Breton trader in Tel Mora if he agrees to sell his goods at the Varo Tradehouse in Vos. I need to bring Aryon a potion of cure paralyzation; he suggested I check Andil's stock in the Service Tower.

I have a special potion from Master Aryon which should cure the Breton trader's curse of paralysis. Aryon asked me to try to convince the trader to go work at the Varo Tradehouse which is in need of a trader. I should return to Tel Mora.

I brought the potion back to the Breton trader, but he figured out that I was only helping him for the reward. I agreed to give him a cut of the reward Master Aryon offered me in the amount of one hundred septims.
I convinced the Breton trader to go to the Varo Tradehouse after I removed his curse of paralysis. I should talk to Master Aryon about my reward.
I brought the potion back to the Breton trader, but he figured out that I was only helping him for the reward and I refused to give him a cut so he said he'd get someone else to help him.

I brought the potion back to the Breton trader, but he figured out that I was only helping him for the reward. I decided to just give him the potion and he thanked and paid me for my help. But I can't expect to get a reward from Master Aryon now.

I brought the potion back to the Breton trader, but he didn't believe me that the potion would only work if he went to work at the tradehouse and when I threatened to hit him with the bottle, he just laughed at me and threatened to call the guards. I can't expect to get a reward from Master Aryon now.
I decided not to give the Breton trader the potion after all. He'll die out there in the cold, but that's not my problem.
Master Aryon thanked me for convincing the Breton trader to work at the Varo tradehouse and gave me a reward for my assistance.
Magical Misdeeds

Alenus Vendu told me that she has had some trouble with her items wandering off. I agreed to help track down who or whatever is responsible. She mentioned that Tel Vos is full of secret passages and strange things and suggested that I look for a hidden way into the Services Tower.

I found the scamp who is responsible for stealing Alenus Vendu's merchandise. It claimed that the "shinies are delicious" which I believe means that it ate them. It became angry and attacked me when I tried to intimidate it into telling me where the items are at now. I should search the area; I have to imagine they wouldn't be far.

I found the scamp who is responsible for stealing Alenus Vendu's merchandise. It claimed that the "shinies are delicious" which I believe means that it ate them. It seemed hostile, so I didn't press for information on the whereabouts of the items. I should search the area; I have to imagine they wouldn't be far.

I found the scamp who is responsible for stealing Alenus Vendu's merchandise. It claimed that the "shinies are delicious" which I believe means that it ate them. I intimidated the scamp and it quickly ran away. I should chase it down and force it to tell me where the items are at now.

After confronting the wretched scamp a second time, I convinced it to give me a passkey to Tel Vos which should allow me access to the room where it hid what remains of the items. It said that it was up the ladder from where I found it.

I have found what's left of Alenus Vendu's merchandise. It appears that they were eaten and then shat into a pile in a hidden room within Tel Vos. They are all completely devoid of enchantment now. I should let her know what I found.

Alenus Vendu was grateful that I solved the mystery of her items wandering off. She gave me a powerful scroll as a reward. But I think the Passkey may be the true reward for this job. I wonder what other secrets it may reveal here in Tel Vos.
A New Mouth for Master Aryon
One of my retainers informed me that a courier arrived from Tel Vos in my absence. She left a letter from Aryon's old Mouth.

I agreed to track down Reynel Uvirith for Galos Mathendis. He believes that she would serve well as a new Mouth for Aryon. She was last seen in Sadrith Mora. He suggested that I start by asking down at the docks of that city.

I learned from a shipmaster in Sadrith Mora that he did see someone who fit Reynel Uvirith's description arrive there by boat. He suggested that I speak to someone in the Mages Guild since he didn't see her leave again by boat.

Someone in the Sadrith Mora Mages Guild told me that Reynel Uvirith headed to Vivec by way of the guild guide. They didn't know or wouldn't tell me where she was headed there. I'll have to ask around.
I heard about a weaponmaster named Ulyno Uvirith who works in the Redoran Canton in Vivec. She might know more about Reynel Uvirith's arrival.
I convinced Reynel Uvirith to become Aryon's Mouth. I should let Galos Mathendis know.
Galos Mathendis thanked me for convincing Reynel Uvirith to be a new Mouth of Aryon. He also mentioned that he needs help with his research.
I refused to help Galos Mathendis locate a new Mouth for Aryon. He was very upset and won't talk to me any longer.
Bed Bandits
Menus Felas in Vos has asked me to find his missing bed. He believes that it is somewhere in the bandit cave of Pinsun. The cave is south down the coast from Vos.
I found Menus Felas's bed in Pinsun. I don't have the means to bring it back to him. But I should let him know.
Menus Felas thanked me for finding his bed. He plans to make arrangement to have a new one delivered.
Rats in Varo Tradehouse
After renting a room at the Varo Tradehouse in Vos, I was woken by a rat while I slept. I should report this to Burcanius Varo, the publican.
Burcanius Varo told me that he has been dealing with a rat problem which started after he ordered a shipment of cheese from Cyrodiil which was subsequently eaten by rats.

Burcanius Varo wishes to acquire a khajiit slave to serve as a rat catcher for his tradehouse. He cannot legally own a slave so he plans to purchase the slave's "freedom" and employ it through indentured servitude.
I delivered the contract to Goler Andrethi. He accepted it and gave me the key to release the slave. I expect Varo wishes me to bring his new "servant" to the tradehouse in Vos.
I brought Burcanius Varo's new servant to his tradehouse. Now would be a good time to ask for a reward.
Burcanius Varo thanked me for bringing him a rat catcher. He rewarded me with a lifetime supply of scuttle. He said that he gets new shipments in once per week.
Burcanius Varo thanked me for letting him know about the rat problem and refunded me for my room.
I refused to help Burcanius Varo purchase the khajiit slave to serve as a rat catcher for him.
The slave Burcanius Varo was interested in serving as his rat catcher died.
I freed the slave which Burcanius Varo purchased to serve as his rat catcher.

I traded with Athanden Girith. Hides for metalworking supplies. But we would never attack a peaceful trader. The ones you are looking for are Emul-Ran and Kashtes Ilabael. They are outcasts, belonging to none of our tribes. You should be able to find them south of here, along the water's edge. May you bring them swift justice.

In the village, the roots break through walls with ease. But they seem weaker here in the egg mine. Some frail tendrils may break through the loose rock, but they quickly wither. I've noticed that the vapors coming from the poisonous acid pools are particularly capable at repelling the roots.

Well, no. It's fairly dangerous to collect. Even a small spray from a forager can blind you. And a whole lake of the stuff is dangerous enough without intentionally trying to skim the cysts off the surface. But if it really worked, then maybe someone desperate enough might be willing to risk it.

Here in town, the roots are a problem -- they even blocked Runethyne's door once. But we rarely see them in the egg mine. And when we do, they wither and retreat quickly. I've never been able to figure it out, but you could talk to my wife, Ibanu, about it. She ventures deeper into the colony than I do. She should be in Sinarralit Egg Mine right now.
It's none of my business.
Intriguing aren't they? The magic used to grow them isn't really my area of expertise, but it makes one wonder what else could grow to enormous sizes with a little magical encouragement...
Not my problem. Aryon grabbing Tel Vos has been great for business.
Settled people always complain about their houses.
The roots in the village? Oh, that is nothing. You should see some Telvanni towns on the mainland, outlander.

The chapel has sustained a lot of damage due to the roots. But at least it doesn't willingly smash my holy icons like the Ashlander savages! I give thanks for Master Aryon every day in my prayers to Almsivi.
Bah. The Villagers can deal with the roots. If they were smart, they'd let Aryon grow them house pods.

Oh I don't mind the roots. The villagers patch the holes they make. But did you know that Telvanni mushroom roots secrete a luminous resin? It's useful in potions to fortify your strength if mixed with ash yams.
Vos? Yes, the town will be fine. The roots won't damage the foundations.
The town is still standing. I do not believe Master Aryon would let the roots destroy it -- and if they did, the villagers could always be housed in mushroom pods.

Dreynos told me about how you helped him with the root problem. I doubt we can collect enough kwama poison to completely eradicate them. And I don't know that I want to. But we may be able to use it on smaller intrusions in sensitive areas. Thank you for helping our village.

I have no solution nor do I know if one even exists. Perhaps you could ask some of the other villagers. They're mostly here in the village; except for the egg miners -- but we rarely see roots in the egg mine. I respectfully ask that you do not bring this up to Master Aryon. We do not wish to appear ungrateful for his protection.

Hard to miss them when you approach our town, isn't it? They're beautiful in a way, but they have an immense power under their knotted surface. Unfortunately, the buildings in our town have suffered some cosmetic damages thanks to the roots. Nothing structurally concerning: mostly walls and roofs caving in which need to be repaired. In general, they follow the path of least resistance and the foundations of this town are strong.
Thanks again for your help. I'll tell everyone in town about what you did. Now we have a solution for our root problem!

The kwama poison worked! It took some time, but I applied more every day and then all of a sudden they withered up and I was able to pull them out and repair my house. Thank you for your help. Here, take this Dwemer goblet I dug up. Safe travels, %PCName.

The kwama poison worked! It took some time, but I applied more every day and then all of a sudden they withered up and I was able to pull them out and repair my house. Thank you so much for your help! Here, take this Dwemer goblet I dug up. When I was looking at it more closely, I noticed a coin stuck to the inside of it by some dirt. Maybe it's valuable? Anyway, you've earned them both. Safe travels, %PCName.
It will take some time for the kwama poison to work on the roots. Come back in a few days.
I don't have much to offer, but there's a Dwemer artifact which I unearthed in the fields. I hope that's enough?
Please hurry! I'm not sure when the roots will sprout more tendrils.
Okay, okay. I was saving this for a rainy day, but I'll give you my last skooma if you'll get the kwama poison for me. I'm desperate.
Fine. You're no better than the raiders. Now get going!

Oh this is such a relief, %PCName. I have high hopes that this will work. I expect that it may take up to a week for the acid to do its work. Come back and talk to me and I'll have something for you to show my thanks.

You say that kwama poison may be the secret to repelling the roots? What an unexpected discovery! Please bring me three samples of these cysts you describe. If it's as potent as Ibanu describes, it should make quick work of the intruders in my house.
Have you gathered the kwama poison cysts like you promised?
Don't come back until you have the kwama poison!
My house is a wreck. Please bring me any news of a possible solution for the mushroom menace.

Here, take my spare key and take a look at the damage yourself. Well, even though this is a common issue, we don't usually discuss solutions at the village meetings. One of Master Aryon's retainers is generally in attendance and it's considered ungrateful to mention the damages. Perhaps if you ask some of my fellow villagers someone will have an idea. I would suggest starting with Hetwoman Kaushad. She's generally in her farmhouse.
Master Aryon offered to grow us some, but we prefer the old Velothi style. It's part of our heritage, %PCName. Surely you can understand.
It is, but I was getting around to asking for your help. I don't have much, but I could offer you a Dwemer artifact I dug up in the fields last season.
Then kindly get out of my fields, outlander.

Master Aryon's construction of Tel Vos was a great thing for Vos. He's a worthier lord than any commoner could ask for. But the roots spreading from his tower are a nuisance. You've seen what they did to our poor town. Not a month goes by that a new tendril doesn't break its way into one of our homes. Just the other night one burst through my wall, upheaving my bed while I was asleep!
I'll take these roots over Ashlander raiders any day.
I've grown accustomed to hearing the groan of the roots growing around my house at night. Do I wish they would stop breaking through my wall? Of course, but what are we supposed to do about it?
Hetwoman Kaushad says that we should be grateful for Master Aryon's protection from Ashlander raiders. And we are, but the roots really are a nuisance.

We deal with roots every day here in the village. They uproot wickwheat in our fields, smash in our walls, but you know I've never heard of them being a problem in the egg mines. Maybe the kwama eat them. Ha!
My men told me that someone had taken care of the ashlander raiders who've been plaguing Vos lately. Here is the reward, as promised. May Stendarr's luck be with you.
Oooo-oh! No, please don't touch us! We don't like popping. Get away from us!
Help! Not the master's poker. Don't bite me with it, please, man-thing! Help!
Help! Help! Put that sword away, nice man-thing. Pleaase!
BAD man-thing! Bite and scratch and chew the TIPS and BITS!
I knew you were a nice man-thing. Act nice and go away!
We swallow shinies. They taste like rats and hunger. But master lets me taste them only, while he eats the souls. It can have them back, they don't smell half so bad as MAN-KIN!
We swallow shinies. They taste like rats and hunger. But master lets me taste them only, while he eats the souls. Man-kin can have them back, they don't smell half so bad as YOU!

Milyn Faram is preoccupied with his research. I expect that he will be spending less time in his tower now that he is rid of the Hlaalu invaders. I expect that there will be some clues as to the device's location in his living area. Find it and report back to me.

The artifact which I seek has the ability to duplicate images onto parchment. Tossing aside the obvious applications already filled by the Imperial printing press, this machine is imbued with dwemer efficiency and I would like to study it more closely. Milyn has worked out a way to create magical scrolls with this device. If you can acquire it for me, then you will be welcome to use it yourself. Still interested?

I have acquired several additions to my dwemer museum. In no small part thanks to your own exploits, %PCName. You have unlocked many hidden secrets of the dwemer during your time here on Vvardenfell. Your report on Odirniran revealed an artifact which I would like to obtain for more than just visitors to gawk at. Might I interest you in revisiting Milyn Faram's tower?
The museum is a hobby of mine.

I overheard Master Aryon speaking to one of his retainers when he last visited to congratulate us on our stewardship of his museum. He mentioned something about a dwemer machine which can create drawings on parchment. You are Telvanni; perhaps he will speak to you of it.

I overheard Master Aryon speaking to one of his retainers when he last visited to congratulate us on our stewardship of his museum. He mentioned something about a dwemer machine which can create drawings on parchment. Perhaps if you were in the House, he would speak to you of it.

The master is always trying to find new artifacts for his museum. He mentioned something during his last visit about an Imperial spymaster in Balmora and his informants being the key to unlocking the depths of Arkngthand.

I don't often hear the master talk about the Imperial guild of mages, but he spoke considerately of a woman in Ald'ruhn named Edwinna Elbert. Apparently another scholar of the deep folk. This one thinks helping her might help the master with his museum.

The master has a friend in Gnisis named Baladas. We heard that he is also a scholar of the deep folk. Perhaps helping him would open up new opportunities for us to find new artifacts for the master's museum.

This one doesn't like Gothren, but his Mouth... well this one doesn't like his Mouth either. But I heard that he is looking for someone to go to a Dwemer ruin. If you do that, I think Aryon might let me go snooping around for museum additions.

The master is a scholar of the deep folk. This museum enshrines his devotion to the pursuit of improvement. We will warn you only once: do not despoil this shrine. It will displease Master Aryon and we will not suffer that.

That's good news, %PCName. I already let Aryon know about my plan and he approved the arrangement. I found a few extra soul gems lying around. Please take them. Oh, and if you have more time, I could use some help with my enchanting research. I'm sure some of the results will be worthy rewards for your efforts.
I take it you have not found Reynel Uvirith yet.
That may be true in part, but it is a very selfish outlook, %PCName. I am sorry that you won't give Master Aryon any credit for his own character in his dealings with you.
%PCName, please. I know you are busy. But think of everything Master Aryon did for you, the rising star of House Telvanni. Do him this one favor in return.

As I said, she made land in Sadrith Mora but left soon thereafter according to my friend. Perhaps if you ask around in the city someone will have seen or heard from her. She's a redhaired Dunmer woman. I expect well-dressed. I would start down at the docks.

As it happens, I already have someone in mind. Her name is Reynel Uvirith. She's from Llothanis Heights on the mainland, but I received word from a friend in Sadrith Mora that she's come to Vvardenfell for reasons unknown to me. She didn't stay in Sadrith Mora long. If I wait for my letters to catch up with her, I'll be at this for another year at least. That's why I need your help.
Wonderful. It's fairly simple, really. [Milar teaches you a self-healing spell and you feel your grasp of restoration increase.] You have natural talent! May you walk in health and security, friend.
Of course. Here you are. Thank you again for your help.

Excellent! Thank you for your help, %PCName! This is enough to make all the potions I need for a while. As a reward, I'll give you a choice: I can teach you some things about restoration and show you a cheap spell of healing that I created or I can give you a package of restorative supplies from my stock.
I'm afraid that isn't quite enough, %PCName. I need 5 portions each of bloat and scrib jelly to make enough potions.
Please don't delay for long, %PCName. I'm not sure how much longer we can tolerate the scaly f'lah.
Have you found enough bloat and scrib jelly? Remember I needed 5 portions of each.

That's wonderful news! Smokeskin-Killer has been getting increasingly irritable without his potions. Don't tell him I told you this, but he's a veteran of the Arnesian War and the horrors of his experience still haunt him. The potions help him fight back the nightmares... Oh! I almost forgot the egg mines. So the two closest are Mudan-Mul and Sinarralit.

I have plenty of wickwheat, but I need more than one ingredient to be able to brew the fortify willpower potions I need. The potions are for Smokeskin-Killer, the Argonian mercenary in Aryon's Dwemer museum. Bloat and scrib jelly both have fortify willpower effects and can conveniently both be found in the nearby kwama egg mines. I need 5 portions of each. Some of the kwama may be aggressive and kwama colonies have other dangers... are you still interested?
Then perhaps I can interest you in some of my services?

In addition to offering magical healing services, I carry restorative supplies which can be used by anyone to mend wounds and treat affliction out in the wild. Speaking of which, I am low on fortify willpower ingredients, maybe you'd be interested in a job?

In addition to offering magical healing services, I carry restorative supplies which can be used by anyone to mend wounds and treat affliction out in the wild. And thanks to you, I have enough bloat and scrib jelly to keep Smokeskin-Killer soothed for a while.

Thank you for getting my hides and guar back. It's good to hear you were able to make those fetchers pay as well. Make sure to see Berwen in Tel Mora for your reward. I'll send word along the trade routes to make sure she keeps an eye out for %PCName.

Thank you for getting my hides and guar back. It's good to hear you were able to make at least one of those fetchers pay as well. Make sure to see Berwen in Tel Mora for your reward. I'll send word along the trade routes to make sure she keeps an eye out for %PCName.

Good to finally have my hides and guar back. Don't know how I would have made it without them. Shame you couldn't get rid of those two Ashlanders, but I thank you for your help. Remember to talk to my friend Berwen in Tel Mora. I'll send word to her to keep an eye out for you, %PCName.
Yes, those bastard Ashlanders took my entire shipment. It's easy to identify mine; they have my mark on them.

Ahhh... my old friend Girith! I heard you helped him out of some serious trouble not long ago. Some business with a couple of no-good Ashlanders, right? They'll never learn. And I heard that you even managed to save his pack guar. Remarkable. Anyway, you have my thanks; I had quite an investment in those guar hides. Would have taken quite a beating had Girith not been able to sell them. Here, take these potions and this powerful ring a token of our appreciation.

Ahhh... my old friend Girith! I heard you helped him out of some serious trouble not long ago. Some business with a couple of no-good Ashlanders, right? They'll never learn. Anyway, you have my thanks; I had quite an investment in those guar hides. Would have taken quite a beating had Girith not been able to sell them. Here, take these potions and this powerful ring a token of our appreciation.
It growled at me when I tried to climb the bookshelf to reach a book on the top. The people here call it a librarian, but I think it wants to eat me.

Maintaining control of a daedra for such a length of time is no small feat. Even after studying the lesser minions of Oblivion for three hundred years, I still could not manage more than a few minutes. A daedra is not some mindless undead reanimation; they are beings with their own agenda. Be careful not to anger Vyassa.

Master Aryon summoned the daedroth to work in the Tel Vos Library here. Why a daedra instead of a retainer? I don't know. Even among other daedra, daedroths are a vain bunch. It gathered some bricks from outside and fashioned itself a throne in the other room. I think it fancies itself the Ruler of the Library.
Oh, so you met the daedra did you? Between you and me, I don't think it can actually read. How does it know where to put the books?
Alenus Vendu has reported the missing items multiple times. But we have not observed anyone entering or leaving the tower during the night hours when she reports they are stolen.
Alenus Vendu has had trouble with items from her shop going missing recently. Tel Vos is a strange place; there could be any number of explanations.
I doubt I'll have any more items wander off now thanks to you.

Ugh... that's disgusting. No, please. I don't want any of it returned. At least I know what to ward against now. I hope you disposed of that wretched creature. Someone needs to tell Aryon that his infatuation with daedra is becoming a problem for us lesser folk. Here, please accept this as a token of my gratitude.
Please let me know straight away if you learn anything about my items wandering off.

I am relieved to hear that. I don't know who is stealing my goods, but I do know that Tel Vos is full of secret passages and strange things. I would suggest you look for a hidden way into this tower. The guards outside should have seen someone skulking through the front doors.
Please reconsider if you find the time.

Oh, I'm such a fool! How did I not consider that before? My wards would keep out a mortal soul such as you or me. Or even a rat. But would have no effect on a daedra or undead spirit. I'll place additional wards down. But I would still like to recover my lost items and confirm who or what is behind the disappearances. Are you willing to help me?

I've placed wards on my goods which should be triggered by any thief. But more items go missing in the morning nonetheless; and with the wards still intact. I even stayed up all night but didn't see a thing. Nothing was stolen either, so I assume whoever it is knew I was there, but I can't stay up every night! I would be willing to offer a handsome reward if you could unravel this mystery for me.

Sinarralit Egg Mine is south of Vos. If you head out through the western gate of the village, then take the southern paths at the first two intersections, and then head east at the third. You'll find the mine entrance at the end of that short path.

Sinarralit Egg Mine is south of Vos. If you take the eastern road towards Vos, take the southern paths at the first two intersections and then head east at the third. You'll find the mine entrance at the end of that short path.
I've heard that there is an ashlander scout staying at the Varo Tradehouse in Vos. I'd like you to speak with her about Indoranyon if you have the time.
I'm still waiting for you to deliver a letter to Milyn Faram.

I received a letter from a fellow scholar of enchantments: Milyn Faram. I know you've been to his tower already, so I'm hoping that you'll agree to deliver a letter to him personally. I would prefer not to risk it with an ordinary courier.

I don't have any more work for you at the moment. I need to focus on my research for a while. I heard that Aryon is trying to expand his Dwemer Museum, maybe you could talk to his guard caretaker, Smokeskin-Killer. I believe that he is hoping someone will take on quests to explore more dwemer ruins so that he can convince Aryon to let him search them for artifacts to bring back to the museum.
There's a book I need to supplement my research. It's called "The Final Lesson".
I still need scamp skin to make scamp tallow.
Back when I was Aryon's Mouth, I didn't have much time for my own research. Now that I'm retired, I have some catching up I'd like to do. First off, I need some scamp tallow.
I don't need any help at the moment.
I'm afraid that I can't work with you until you rejoin House Telvanni.
Come outlander. Let us find the Mer-Eater Nix-Hound!
The monster will tremble at the sight of us!
More dangerous to ignore the danger!
I will wait for a willing companion on my quest to defeat the beast.
The monster must be stopped! Will you come with me and face it?
I can feel the seething hunger of the beast is gone from my dreams. Thank you for killing it, %PCName.

This beast has been here for some time. It intrudes on my dreams and visions and grows stronger with every spirit it consumes. Our hunters have not been able to find it. I believe it has become very cunning to evade capture. A dangerous beast indeed.
Take care, outlander. Creatures who feed on merflesh should not be treated lightly.
Thank you for destroying that foul beast, %PCName. Whenever a wild animal tastes human flesh, it must be hunted without delay.
Kintus Yanudadammu was the previous resident of Menus Felas's farmhouse. He went missing some time ago. He wasn't a hunter though.

I'm glad to hear that the nix-beast is dead. Nix-hounds are typically content to scavenge for scraps outside of camps and towns. But occasionally one is emboldened by the smell of vulnerable spirits and will attack. Consuming the body and spirit of the victim and becoming even more powerful and cunning. I am pleased that you managed to end this insatiable cycle.
So there was some truth to that notice after all, eh? Makes you wonder what to believe.

Drink in those notices with a grain of salt, %PCClass. I try to take down the junk when I have the time. But I don't have much time. People do go missing around here, but it's mostly blamed on the raiders.
Ashlanders have superstitions about beasts devouring the body and spirit of people and becoming something unholy. Faith in Almsivi would save them from this fear.
The hunter turned INTO a nix-hound? You would be wise to keep this tale to yourself, %PCName. You'll earn a visit from the inquisition if an Ordinator hears you say that.
I never met Kintus Yanudadammu. But a few people have reported large creatures -- not just nix-hounds -- in the grazelands. It's a dangerous place. Don't be fooled by the idyllic appearance.

Wild animals consuming people's spirits together with their flesh and gradually becoming something more than animal is a common motif in Ashlander folk tales... Mere superstitions of course, but the Waste Folk take it very seriously and immediately dispose of maneaters in their territory.
The rumors about a large nix-hound preying on people have not been confirmed. But be watchful on the roads at night, %PCRace. We can't save you from every stray beast.
I've seen something slinking through the grass at night. Looked like an enormous nix-hound to me.
I saw Kintus just a few weeks ago. He was out on a hunting trip. I'm surprised he has the guts to go after a Mer-Eater Nix-Hound.

A Mer-Eater Nix-Hound? It needs to be killed. Else none of our dreams will be safe. You should speak to Maela Kaushad. She used to be a Wise Woman and knows how to deal with nix-beasts. Or go talk to the ashlanders.
Kintus left to go back to nomad life with the Ashlanders. Maybe he became a hunter.
Maela told me that Kintus was probably killed by wild animals. But I saw him a few months ago. Must be living in one of the Ashlander camps in the region.
Mudan-Mul Egg Mine is due west of Tel Vos. You can take the south road, then take a right at the fork, then follow the northerly route until you see the entrance.

You cured the queen. Master Aryon opened the mine again. Red dust from Red Mountain no longer sickens the beasts here. It will be many years more before the colony fully recovers. But they seem to recognize your musk and do not attack. That is a good sign.
Thank you for convincing the Breton trader to come work at the Varo Tradehouse. Ferise and Burcanius will take care of him.
Thank you for convincing the Breton trader to come work at the Varo Tradehouse. Ferise and Burcanius will take care of him. As promised, here is a fitting reward for your assistance.
It's disappointing that you failed to convince the trader to come to Vos, but I knew it wasn't a sure thing.
I already gave you the potion.

Let me see that potion. Here you go, %PCRank. Please remember to ask the trader to come to the Varo Tradehouse. If you can convince him, I can reward you for your efforts. Just come back to Tel Vos and talk to me any time.

Let me see that potion. There, that should do it. Now, before you go, please remember to ask the trader to come to the Varo Tradehouse. If you are successful, come talk to me again and I'll give you an appropriate reward.
This will do, thank you, %PCName. Just give me a moment to add this to the potion...
I'll make some changes to the cure paralyzation potion when you bring it to me.
Given the extenuating circumstances, I will. Bring me a potion of cure paralyzation. Andil in the Services Tower might have one.

So Dratha cursed another man that wandered into her tower, did she? Normally I wouldn't interfere in such a trifling matter, but you say he is a trader? Well, Burcanius Varo, the proprietor of the Varo Tradehouse in Vos, has been looking for someone to bring some trade to his tradehouse. We don't get many peddlers this far from the big cities so he's gotten rather desperate and I think he would accept just about anyone at this point.
That poor man-elf; he was found dead in the street. I wish I could have helped.
I'm happy to hear that Master Aryon agreed to help that poor man-elf.
Like I said, maybe Master Aryon will help. You'll need to go talk to him in Tel Vos.

Oh, that poor man-elf. I'm afraid that only a very powerful wizard could remove that curse from him now. Mistress Dratha will not be persuaded; we have seen this before, unfortunately. But the lord of Tel Vos, Master Aryon, is a much milder ruler and Tel Vos is just across the channel. You can take the boat there. Perhaps if you talk to Master Aryon, he will be willing to help this foolish trader.
That man got what he deserved. My guards carried him out of town like a marshmerrow reed.
Would the little man like a curse of his own?
I try not to think about it.
Please, what is it you want? Money? I can pay you. Just please, please give me the potion!
Curse you!
Ah, thank you, %PCName. You have no idea how good this feels. Here, take this as payment. And yes, I will go to work at this tradehouse. I don't know if it will last, but I'll give it a shot.

Ah, thank you, %PCName. You have no idea how good this feels. I'm sorry, but I won't be going to that tradehouse. I can't stand these Telvanni. I'm taking the next boat out of here. But here, take this small payment as a sign of my gratitude.
Ah, thank you, %PCName. You have no idea how good this feels. Yes, I will go to work at this tradehouse. I don't know if it will last, but I'll give it a shot.
Pleasure doing business with you, %PCName. I'll go to the tradehouse after you give me the potion...
You don't have enough coin, %PCRace. Come back when you'e ready to deal.
Fine, I'll get someone else to help me then. Leave.
Why? What's in it for you? Tell you what, give me one hundred septims and I'll go to this tradehouse. I'm no fool. If you want you're reward, then I want a cut.
Ha! You don't look like you could hurt a rat. How about I call the guards over here? They want me to die slowly after all. Wander off, %PCRace.
No, please! Okay, okay, I'll go to this tradehouse, just calm down and give me the potion...
A potion with stipulations? What do you take me for? I'm a Breton, not an Orc; potions don't work that way. Now are you going to dump that potion down my throat or leave me here to die?

I know you're right... I shouldn't be so quick to judge. But talk about getting off on the wrong foot! If Master Aryon is as admirable as you say, then I'm sure I'll be content at this tradehouse. Can I have the potion now?

How dare you insult me like that!... but you're right, I only came out here because I wasn't having any luck in the Hlaalu and Redoran towns. I suppose I could give it a try at this tradehouse. Can I have the potion now?
You want me to go sell my wares in a Telvanni tradehouse? Are you crazy? These spore-huffing elves are all insane!
Please, hurry!
Have you managed to find anyone who can help me? I think my toes might hurt if I could feel them!
I can't remove it myself. Maybe someone in town will have an idea. Kirsty right there in the housepod brought me some food yesterday. Maybe she'll help.
That Breton broke the law of the mage-lord. Do not interfere.
I don't want to get involved, sorry.

The workers never informed me that they installed a valve... thank you for your help, %PCName. It was quite... providential that you came around and solved this issue for me. I believe that a proper thanks is in order. Normally I prefer to give a choice in rewards, but I happened to have this nearby and I think it suits the situation admirably.
One of my retainers informed me that the water is functioning in my conservatory again. I assume that you had something to do with it?

I commissioned the conservatory to serve as a place of respite amidst all the responsibilties I am tied to. And now the water lies still. If I hadn't inspected the pump myself, I'd have suspected tampering from a fellow councilor...
I wouldn't ask you to deal with my plumbing issues, %PCName. But since you're offering, yes, I would greatly appreciate if you could find out why my conservatory water stopped.
With that attitude, you'll fit right into House Telvanni.
The water in my conservatory stopped flowing recently. My retainers can't determine where the fault lies and the fools who installed the machinery never put in a valve.

Thank you for your assistance in acquiring the device for me. Even if you did botch the sneaking around. Everything turned out for the better. I hear that Milyn Faram is creating a regular compound out of Odirniran.

The ideographer has been installed in my laboratory which is located at the top of the second tallest tower. You are free to use it whenever you like. You can buy some standard blank scrolls from Alenus Vendu in the Services Tower. You'll need them to run through the machine. I've left some notes down in the lab which Milyn sent with the machine.
The device is not set up yet. Come back in a few days.

Milyn caught you did he? He's as shrewd as a Hlaalu... but his offer is acceptable to me. I'll make arrangements to have the device moved here. Come see me in a week and I expect that everything should be set up.

Milyn Faram is dead? That is highly disappointing, %PCName. Now it will take years to reiterate his research. Not to mention that House Hlaalu will quickly move to inhabit Odirniran. Thereby making the acquisition of the dwemer ideographer nearly impossible. This is a great loss for House Telvanni.

You may ask why would I not just scrawl out images of daedra onto parchment rather than using that bulky machine? Well, the reasons boil down to quality, %PCName. In order for the summoning to work, the image has to be an incredibly accurate representation of the target. That's why most enchanters use actual pieces of the daedra to establish this link.

The book has been very useful, %PCName. Thank you again.
I'd be happy to. Here, let's look at something you may have missed in this book. [Galos teaches you some things about enchanting from "The Final Lesson"].

You've certainly earned it. Here you are. I found this creature wandering around the Southern Tower and managed to kill it and trap its soul. Some type of scaly rat. It might have wandered up from the passages below the tower -- but I haven't seen anything like it around here before.

You have a copy of the book? Wonderful! I can feel a breakthrough approaching in my research. As compensation for your work, what would you like? I could teach you something about enchanting? Or perhaps you'd prefer a soul gem I filled recently?
I hope you haven't gotten into too much trouble trying to obtain a copy of "The Final Lesson" for me. House Telvanni is fairly forgiving of transgressions if you make amends.

Of course. It's fairly simple to make a small amount of light bend around you... [Galos teaches you a simple chameleon spell]. And that's it. Please let me know if you succeed in obtaining a copy of the book for me.
Of course. Please let me know if you succeed in obtaining a copy of the book for me.

I have seen two copies recently. One in Gothren's tower in Tel Aruhn and another owned by Endar Drenim in Neloth's tower, Tel Naga, in Sadrith Mora. I didn't plan to send you unprepared, however. Take this Scroll of Invisibility that I made. A chameleon effect may be more useful, but I'm no illusionist. I do know a very low level chameleon spell if you'd like to learn the effect though.
What? Have you been reading my notes? Well... thank you, %PCName.

The book deals with some enchanting topics that I am interested in. Unfortunately, I have not had the opportunity to study it in quite some time and it is rather difficult to acquire. Normally, I would wait for my order to be fulfilled with a bookseller, but age has made me impatient. So I'm asking you to steal a copy for me. What do you say?
He is the guard and caretaker of my Dwemer Museum. He's a good friend, but certainly not a scholar.
Yesss?
He's a skilled warrior with a troubled past. I try to help him out how I can.
He's patrolling the Dwemer Museum. He's been in a much better mood lately. Hasn't called me a "smokeskin" in a threatening way in at least a week.
He's patrolling the Dwemer Museum. He's been in a much better mood lately.
He's patrolling the Dwemer Museum. I wouldn't try talking to him right now though. Milar Maryon usually brings some potions that cheer him up. But he hasn't in a while that I have noticed anyway.
You'll find him in the central tower.
No, thank you.

Ordinary keys unlock ordinary doors, correct? Yes, well some doors are not ordinary. So they require extraordinary keys with particular imbuements. The enchantment isn't important, but words of power are. It's all theoretical at this point and I know this might not make much sense. There are still some pieces of the puzzle that are missing.
As a matter of fact, I just learned of a visitor in town that I'd like you to speak with about my enchanting research.
Oh yes, thank you! This is just what I needed. Here, I made this amulet for practice, but don't really need it. Maybe you'll have a use for it. Or sell it, I'm not sentimental.

I hear more from Tel Vos nowadays than Sadrith Mora or Port Telvannis combined. But give me the letter. Yes, I see. Galos isn't expecting a written response. So just tell him that I understand. Oh, and give this to him.
Please be careful with that letter. We Telvanni are very protective of our research. I've dedicated my entire life to the topics disclosed within.
Thank you, %PCName. You've been invaluable in assisting with my research. Here is the letter. Encoded of course -- I've learned a thing or two from Aryon, you see.

As you already know, Milyn Faram has a particular interest in the creation of magical scrolls. Though he does dabble in several other pursuits as well... we've been trading notes on our particular research topics for some time. If you are willing, I'll give you my letter to deliver to him. He tells me that he's made changes to that old Velothi tower thanks to Aryon's investment in the dwemer ideographer.
I'm not here to flip pages, %PCRace. But you're welcome to peruse Master Aryon's library. Just don't take anything or the daedroth might bite your head off if I don't get to you first.

When I am not out performing field research, I am typically here. Master Aryon has quite the collection of books. Enough for years of study. And he is generous to allow his underlings nearly unrestricted access to it. More than can be said of most mage-lords.

You're in the library. Master Aryon moved his collection of books with him when he built his tower here. Now he lets the locals and House Telvanni retainers such as myself utilize the books for our own studies. I think he keeps the best for himself, but I'm not complaining.
Master Aryon lets us folk from Vos come look at the books in his library. Many of us have even learned to read!
Reynel is my cousin. She can tell you why she is here.
The only Uvirith I know about is Ulyno. She's a Master-At-Arms at the Scout and Drillmaster in the Redoran Waistworks.
What's it to you, Telvanni? Leave me be.
An Uvirith from House Telvanni here in Vivec? No, I don't know of any. There is an Ulyno Uvirith in the Redoran Canton. A weaponmaster from what I hear. You might try asking her.
No Uvirith's from House Telvanni here in Vivec, %PCRank.
No Uvirith's from House Telvanni here in Vivec.
I didn't see anyone with red hair and haven't heard that name before. But a Dunmer woman in a hooded purple robe did come here. She hurried out quickly. I'm not sure where she was headed.
I didn't notice anyone with that description.
I've not seen anyone with that description, %PCRace.
I don't know her, sorry. But Vivec is a big place.
No I haven't seen anyone like that.
A woman by that name did come here seeking guide service. I didn't tell you this, but she was headed to Vivec,
What? You think I'm going to tell some nosy outlander what she did heret?
It's against guild policy to discuss client activity.

A redhaired Telvanni noblewoman? Aye, a lady arrived with that description recently. She didn't leave from the docks, though. So if she's no longer here, as you say, then I reckon she must've used the Mages Guild service. Not like she was going to hike anywhere in that fancy purple robe of 'er's.
Most of the Uvirith famiy are back on the mainland. No one here in Sadrith Mora that I know of.
Thanks for tracking her down for me. She's already representing Master Aryon in Sadrith Mora.

I saw you blink when I mentioned her name, %PCName. Yes, her family is the namesake for your tower. I don't know the whole story or how closely she is related to whichever "Uvirith" was buried there. Perhaps she will tell you herself.

%Name helped build tower. Knows of many, many secrets. Unfinished tower towards setting sun has metal ring to pull. Leads to secret place. There are more secret places. Look for walls which are not walls and floors which are not floors. What a strange place. %Name will not miss it.

Have you visited the Tel Vos Dwemer Museum? Master Aryon has filled it with many strange dwarf-made artifacts. Last time I visited, his museum guard, Smokeskin-Killer, was looking for a Telvanni who might be able to help acquire some new contraption. I didn't understand the details.

Have you visited the Tel Vos Dwemer Museum? Master Aryon has filled it with many strange dwarf-made artifacts. Last time I visited, his museum guard, an Argonian, was looking for a Telvanni who might be able to help with something. He wouldn't divulge the details with me.

Have you visited the Tel Vos Dwemer Museum? Master Aryon has filled it with many strange dwarf-made artifacts. Smokeskin-Killer, the caretaker, is always trying to get people to go on missions into Dwemer ruins. Apparently Aryon doesn't like sending him in if it hasn't already been explored.
I heard that the enchanter in Tel Vos has been having problems with items "walking off". Sounds like there's a thief in the tower to me. Probably one of those outlander mercenaries.
I heard that Alenus Vendu, the enchanter, has been having problems with items "walking off". Some thieving Ashlander if you ask me.

House Hlaalu has made a move to build trade relations with the Zainab Ashlander tribe. Aryon's captain, Turedus Talanian, is looking for someone to turn this to benefit Tel Vos. With how well you handled the Ashlander nomads the first time, I'm sure he would welcome your help again.

The lantern is a physical manifestation of the ancestor spirit's link to the otherworld. The dream world of the dead. While they possess it, they can roam Sunna Guradan -- or the Grazelands as the settled people call it -- freely. But if they lose it, they will be doomed to wander until they descend into madness and must be banished.
We see the ancestors carrying them across the grazelands on rare occasions. I do not know if it is a sacred or cursed thing that you acquired one. You should speak to a wise woman.

The settled people call this place the Grazelands. This name is fitting as our herds feed off of the rich grass which grows in the dark soil here. However, to us, this land is much more significant than just fertile grasslands. These are the blessed lands of life and greenery. This is how we envision the afterlife appears to our ancestors. And as a Wise Woman, I have dreamt of the otherworld and can tell you that our ancestors believe much the same.

Sunna Guradan are the blessed lands. The settled people and outlanders call them the grazelands. That name is fitting as well, but does carry the same sacred meaning. Our ancestors walk among us and bless us with life and favor.
Thank you for dealing with the Flame Monarch under Tel Vos.

That blade is remarkable -- perhaps you will let me study it one day. With that, I believe you have succeeded in slaying the Flame Monarch. Thank you for your assistance. In return, I offer discounted rates from all of my retainers' services and these potions. I had something else in mind for them, but I think they will make an adequate reward instead.
You say you have banished the Flame Monarch? Bring me a token from his refuge to prove your deed. Powerful daedra are known to keep strong artifacts nearby.

Monarchs are atronachs which are much more powerful than their kin. I won't bore you with the details of why some daedra are more potent than others -- suffice to say atronach monarchs are extremely rare. Flame Monarchs in particular are known to be incurably vainglorious. Reveling in the acclaim of mortals who are terrified by their fearsome appearance. Do not cower before the flame monarch or you will only embolden it.

Atronach monarchs are unholy agents of Oblivion, %PCName. Aryon said that I should offer you free training, but instead I will give you something much more valuable. I will pray to Almsivi on your behalf. May the Three watch over you.

Flame Monarchs are no trivial threat, %PCName. Aryon sent me a note to give you this ring. But my advice to you is to trap the Flame Monarch's soul! You don't run across a daedra that powerful every day. So take these too.
Master Aryon has sent you to banish a Flame Monarch? I have been authorized to provide you with some bandages. I don't expect I'll see you or the bandages again.
You plan to fight a Flame Monarch for Master Aryon? Take these potions. But talk to Milar when you come back without any hair.
Master Aryon was my patron before I retired. He lives here in Tel Vos.
The master is not like other smokeskins. He is devious, but fair to his retainers and subjects. We serve him willingly.

The candles surrounding an enchanter's table aren't just for show. Skilled enchanters can use the aura cast by particular candles to create better enchantments. In the West -- especially in High Rock -- magetallow is frequently used. And some Telvanni use it as well. But scamp tallow candles are almost as powerful and much more... tastefully acquired. Scamp tallow is rendered from the fat left clumped under scamp skin. Magetallow, well, I'll let you think about how it is made.

That looks like enough scamp skin, %PCName. Thank you very much. Here's some gold to cover your expenses. I have some more enchanting research you can help me with while you wait for me to finish the candles. If you're still interested, of course.
I need ten scraps of scamp skin to render enough tallow to make some higher quality candles for my enchanting table.

I think I can render enough tallow from ten scraps of scamp skin. Felara Andrethi in Tel Aruhn generally has some in stock. Otherwise, I would suggest hunting scamp in Daedric shrines or here in the Grazelands where you'll occassionally find them wandering.
Scamp tallow is rendered from the fat left clumped under scamp skin. Magetallow, well, I'll let you think about how it is made.

In the West -- especially in High Rock -- magetallow is frequently used. And some Telvanni use it as well. But scamp tallow candles are almost as powerful and much more... tastefully acquired.

I heard about how you dealt with the Flame Monarch underneath Tel Vos. Makes my skin crawl that it was living right under my boots. That must have been what caused the incident in the dungeon which killed the construction crew.

I don't know if you've ventured down into the dungeon, but I wouldn't recommend it. Something foul took place down there and Master Aryon hasn't restarted the excavation since. There was a cave in and most of the contracting crew was killed.
We have already spoken of this. We will trade with House Hlaalu in Vos. We do not wish to lose warriors in the fire lands.

You speak wisdom. I am glad that you chose to visit us again, %PCName. The Zainab are not pack guar for House Hlaalu. We will demand that all ebony trade take place in Vos to save our warriors the trip through the fire lands.

You have failed your quest and the spirit has gone mad. This is a sad day. I can see now that the ancestor's favor was misplaced in you. Please leave.

You have been tasked with taking a ghost lantern to Molaguradan. Do not set the lantern down for any reason until you have completed your quest.
Please retrieve it and come back here so that we may speak.

Very well, %PCName. You are now tasked with guiding the soul of the Salkurnudai hunter back to the otherworld. You must hold the lantern from here to your destination. Do not set it down, even for a moment, or the ancestor will be lost. Your destination is the burial caverns of Molaguradan. It now lies under the tower of the Telvanni lord in Tel Vos. You will find a river of lava falling into a dark hole. Follow that path.
I am disappointed by your decision, but I will settle the spirit myself.

These roaming ancestors will typically be seen carrying a lantern such as yours. %PCName, it is essential that the lantern returns to the otherworld. Otherwise the spirit you met will be trapped in the waking world and be driven mad. I can perform the necessary rituals of sending, but the ancestor chose to appear to you for a reason. You should be the one to put it back to rest. Will you accept this burden?

You met an ancestor, %PCName. A sacred and serious demonstration of favor. That lantern you found, we call it a ghost lantern. On occasion, our ancestors will walk the blessed lands of Sunna Guradan in flesh by their own volition. This land is pleasant for them and free of any mortal chill which they shun. Sometimes they long for the warm breeze of Red Mountain to touch their skin again.
You met an ancestor, %PCName. A sacred and serious demonstration of favor. That lantern you found, we call it a ghost lantern. Where is it now?

I have never heard that name uttered in the waking world, %PCName. Yes, I know it. The Salkurnudai were an ancient tribe who lived in these lands before the sea divided us. Where did you hear it?
I do not know that name. Talk to a wise woman, they walk the ancestral trail. I can tell you that is a ghost lantern which you carry, outlander. Handle it with respect and bring it to the wise woman.
I do not know that name. Talk to a wise woman, they walk the ancestral trail.
Thank you again for informing me of the ashlanders' desire to regain access to Molaguradan.

Thank you. I hope to see you again with your skin intact, %PCName. I do not wish to lead you to your death unwittingly, however. So I will repeat again: this daedra is a foe most foul. Do not enter into combat with it lightly. I suggest visiting my retainers in the services tower to seek appropriate equipment. And one more thing: bring me a token to prove your deed. I believe you will know it when you see it. Powerful daedra are known to keep strong artifacts nearby.

It has come to my attention that the excavation work underneath my tower has come to a halt due to the meddling of a very dangerous fire daedra known as a Flame Monarch. I can compensate you appropriately if you are willing to banish it.
Very well. I will have to deal with it myself.

Is that so? Thank you for bringing me this information, %PCName. The fact that you thought to tell me shows that you anticipated I would find it valuable. Take this as compensation and with my thanks.

Is that so? Thank you for bringing me this information, %PCName. The fact that you thought to tell me shows that you anticipated I would find it valuable. Take this as compensation and with my thanks. While you are here, there is another issue concerning Molaguradan that you may be able to help me with.
I hope that conversation was worth your trip up here, %PCName.
Yes, I was aware that there was an old ashlander burial site under this hill. Why do you bring it up?

In ancient times, Molaguradan was a burial place for several tribes which lived in the area, including the Salkurnudai. In modern times, we entomb our dead by other means, but the fiery caverns of Molaguradan are still a sacred place. Unfortunately, we do not have access to the caverns now that the Telvanni lord built his tower atop it.
Leave me to my work then, would you?
Sorry, friend. I'm all out of surplus raw ebony. Come back next week and we'll do business.
A pleasure to do business with you, friend. Be sure to stop by again.
That's not enough gold. You're not trying to shortchange me, are you, %PCName?
Back for some more discounted raw ebony, %PCName? I have more to spare. And more again every week new shipments arrive from the ashlanders.
You've got a keen ear for doing business, %PCName. I can only spare 5 pieces per week. But at this price, you can't go wrong!

It's an open secret that I'm moving copious amounts of ebony for House Hlaalu through this port. But what isn't common knowledge is that handling fees drastically increase the cost of any good. Every time it changes hands, the price goes up. See? The raw ebony I have in my possession is close to source -- and I don't mind telling you the ashlanders are selling it to us for a song -- so I can offer you a discount on a small portion of it. Just 100 septims per piece. What do you say?
More the adventuring type, eh? It's no skin off my nose. But leave me to my work then, would you?
That's why I'm here, %PCName. Important business for House Hlaalu. Maybe you'd be interested in a little transaction of your own?
He is serving admirably. I'm confident that we've seen the last of any rats in my tradehouse.
That'll teach me to trust an incompetent adventuring type to escort a single person down a hill... let's just drop the subject.
You're here, but my servant is not. What did you do, %PCName? If I find out that you freed him... well, you wouldn't be my first bad investment. But you're no longer welcome here.

I see my new servant is with you, %PCName. I know this was a menial task for an adventurer like you. So I did some thinking while you were away and I came up with the perfect reward for your troubles! I'm prepared to offer you a lifetime supply of scuttle. I get new shipments every week. Just stop by and I'll have some for your eating pleasure.

This contract reeks of Imperial equivocation. But everything appears to be in order. Here is the key to the slave's... err the servant's bracer. It will also unlock the cell door. I'm not running a delivery service, so you'll have to take the khajiit to Varo yourself.

Varo informed me that he had an interest in the slave we're holding. Master Aryon isn't overly interested in keeping slaves around -- he prefers mercenaries and paid workers. But the contractor working on the tower had a few in his employ before the incident. This one was caught hoarding Dwemer artifacts unearthed during their excavation of the dungeon. Let me see the paperwork Varo sent with you.

I sent word ahead to Goler Andrethi that I was interested in purchasing the slave. Should be no surprise. You'll find them both down in the Tel Vos Jail.
Keep your innocence then, %PCName. Perhaps one day you'll come to realize how the real world operates. I would give that khajiit a purpose and hope for a better future.

Running a tradehouse is a full time commitment, %PCName. I can barely break myself away for long enough to keep my wife from spending every septim I earn while my back is turned. All I'm asking is that you take this contract to the jailer in Tel Vos. A Dunmer by the name of Goler Andrethi. Tell him that I am interested in purchasing the slave's freedom in exchange for ten years servitude. It's all written down.

Well, with cats and dogs being so scarce in this region of Tamriel, something else came to mind. Did you know that some Telvanni actually keep Khajiit slaves to catch rats and other vermin? They're natural hunters. And a side benefit is that they can feed them less. Now, being an Imperial colonist, I am not legally allowed to own a slave, but indentured servitude is common and perfectly legal in the empire. It just so happens that there's a candidate nearby. A Khajiit slave imprisoned in Tel Vos.

Back in Cyrodiil, I owned a dog to keep the vermin out of my tavern. But that was before I decided to join the Imperial colonists headed to Vvardenfell. You don't see many dogs here in Morrowind -- or cats for that matter. Apparently the Dark Elves actually domesticated some larger breeds of rats and trained them as ratters. Fascinating, isn't that? But I have another idea. Maybe something you can help me with.
Thank you for helping me.

So bandits stole my bed? I knew it! Nevermind that bed, I'll have Berwen send me a new one. You didn't think I'd want to sleep on that thing after they took it? Disgusting... But thank you so much for helping. Here, I was going to donate this to the temple, but I want you to have it. Oh, and feel free to take the eggs on the chest of drawers. I hate kwama eggs.
Get out!
Please hurry! My back hurts.

Actually yes. I spoke with the ashlander scout in the tradehouse about bandit hideouts in the area. She told me about a cavern named "Pinsun" south along the coast from here. Right along the shipping lanes from Sadrith Mora. I think the bed bandits will be there.
May the Four Corners curse you. N'wah!
What? Please don't hurt me! Here, take this and leave!
I'll call for the guards if you try anything. Get out of my house!

Oh you saw my notice? Thank the Three! You see, I just moved here from Vivec and I have been sleeping on the floor. With all the time an adventurer like you spends in the wild, surely you can relate to how uncomfortable that is. Anyway, I ordered a bed from Berwen in Tel Mora, but it hasn't arrived yet. It was supposed to be shipped from Sadrith Mora. I fear that it has been accosted by bed bandits!
I don't have time to talk right now, %PCName. Too much work to do.
Oh, %PCName is wise. Guards will see. Take %Name out of the city.
%Name will follow %PCName.

My apologies, %PCName. I didn't mean to be rude, Milyn has been my research partner for a long time. But you have been instrumental to my enchanting research. I have reached the culmination of my studies with just one final step I must take. I must return to my chambers and prepare. Come to Tel Vos in one week's time. I don't have time to explain everything, but I will have something for you then.
I have taken precautions, and I will take more. Even if I fail, I will survive. I must know the answer and pass through the door.
You know what I have to use, Milyn.
Ah, Milyn, I'm glad you could make it. See, it's just as I described. A key is required. Just like with my experiment.

%PCName, don't be alarmed. I'm communicating with you via telepathy. A skill occasionally used by conjurers to link minds. Aryon may have foregone your training as his Mouth, but your formal induction into the role and the time we've spent working together on my research allowed me to establish a weak whisplink with you. Just like Masters do with their Mouths on the council. It appears that you did not mark a location near enough to Indoranyon. I will have to correct for this myself... go to Indoranyon now.

No time for talk. Leave us.

I collect eggs, I am paid. I talk with you, I receive nothing. Leave me to my work, outlander.

Do you have business here, outlander? Mind yourself. This egg mine is the property of Master Aryon.
I'm busy, outlander.
What want? We give manflesh tower-key. Master will find us... master will not be pleased. It stinking man-thing's fault! Want bite! Want POP its arms. Off.

We'll tell it where we put shinies. Don't hurt. Bite. Stab! Up the ladder. Not through glowing door. But THROUGH glowing door, yes. Yes! It must be special tower-friend. We know way. We show nice man-thing way. Take. Read. Now LEAVE!
Eyuh? How find us? Manflesh be nice? We'll be nice. SURE! Its better not touch shinies. Precious shinies are delicious.
NASTY mankin! Die! Now!
